habitat: Coniferous and mixed forests, often near paths
key_warnings: Beware of staining yellow at the base; can be confused with toxic Agaricus species.
cap_description: Large (10-25cm), convex to flat; covered in dense, brown concentric scales on a pale background.
gill_description: Free, crowded; initially white, turning pink then dark chocolate brown with age.
stem_description: Tall (10-20cm), thick, white; features a large, persistent, skirt-like ring.
lookalikes: Agaricus xanthodermus (stains bright yellow, smells of phenol/ink).
environment_tips: Check for proximity to spruce or pine; often found in leaf litter or needles near path edges.

key_warnings: Causes severe gastrointestinal distress. Stains bright yellow when bruised, smells like ink/phenol.
cap_description: Medium (5-15cm), white to off-white, often square-ish in profile when young; stains yellow when scratched.
gill_description: Free, crowded; pinkish-grey becoming dark brown; never remains white.
stem_description: White, bulbous base; stains immediate chrome yellow at the base when cut or bruised.
smell: Unpleasant, like ink, phenol, or library paste.
lookalikes: Edible Agaricus arvensis (stains yellow slowly, smells of anise).
environment_tips: Commonly found in man-made environments like lawns and compost heaps after rain.

key_warnings: Must be cooked thoroughly. easily confused with deadly Amanitas; flesh bruises reddish.
cap_description: Convex to flat (5-15cm), dull yellow to reddish-brown; covered in small, tan warts.
gill_description: Free, white; may develop reddish spots where bruised or with age.
stem_description: White to pinkish, with a bulbous base and a white, skirt-like ring; bruises red.
lookalikes: Amanita pantherina (highly toxic, lacks reddish bruising, has distinct 'booted' volva).
environment_tips: Look for oak or pine trees; check for red staining in insect-damaged areas of the stem.

key_warnings: Likely contains toxins; avoid. Yellow-brown cap with yellow warts.
cap_description: Convex (6-15cm), dark yellow-brown; covered in bright yellow, felt-like warts.
gill_description: Free, white to creamy; crowded and soft.
stem_description: Pale yellow, becoming darker at the base; features a delicate, yellow-tinted ring.
lookalikes: None significant, but the yellow warts on brown cap are a key warning sign for Amanitas.
environment_tips: Found under hemlock and Douglas-fir; watch for yellow veil fragments on the cap margin.

key_warnings: Often confused with edible species. Has a distinct "cleft" or split bulb at the base.
cap_description: Convex (5-12cm), brownish to grey-brown, often with dark radial fibers; may have white patches.
gill_description: Free, white, turning brownish with age or where bruised.
stem_description: White, staining brown; base has a prominent bulb with a vertical 'cleft' or split.
lookalikes: Amanita phalloides (deadly, olive cap, non-split bulb).
environment_tips: Check the base of the stem for the vertical split in the bulb, a critical identification feature.

habitat: Mixed forests (especially with madrone and fir)
key_warnings: Often eaten, but extreme caution advised due to resemblance to deadly Amanitas. Thick patch on cap.
cap_description: Large (10-25cm), orange-brown to yellow; usually has one thick, white patch of veil.
gill_description: Free, white to pale cream; crowded and broad.
stem_description: Thick, white; features a large sac-like volva at the base and a fragile ring.
smell: Mild when young, becoming slightly unpleasant with age.
lookalikes: Amanita phalloides (deadly, usually lacks the single thick patch, has olive-green tones).
environment_tips: Almost always associated with Madrone or Douglas-fir on the West Coast.

habitat: Acidic soils in deciduous and coniferous forests
key_warnings: Contains mild toxins; smells strongly of raw potato.
cap_description: Convex to flat (5-10cm), pale lemon yellow to white; often has irregular, brownish patches.
gill_description: Free, white to pale yellow; crowded.
stem_description: White, with a distinct, sharply-edged bulb at the base and a pale yellow ring.
smell: Strong and distinctive smell of raw potatoes.
lookalikes: Amanita phalloides (deadly, lacks potato smell, has a sac-like volva).
environment_tips: Check the bulb at the base; it should be 'abrupt' with a narrow gutter around the stem.

habitat: Mixed woods (often near hemlock or oak)
key_warnings: Known as the "Yellow Patches" mushroom; do not consume.
cap_description: Convex (3-9cm), bright yellow to orange-yellow; covered in small, bright yellow warts.
gill_description: Free, white to pale yellow; edges may be finely fringed.
stem_description: Yellowish, slender; base is slightly bulbous with yellow powdery remnants; features a fragile ring.
lookalikes: Amanita muscaria var. guessowii (larger, has more prominent concentric rings on the bulb).
environment_tips: Commonly found near hemlock trees in mossy areas or leaf litter.

key_warnings: Contains muscimol and ibotenic acid. Causes severe nausea and delirium. Do not ingest.
cap_description: Large (10-20cm), bright red to orange; covered in white to yellowish pyramidal warts.
gill_description: Free, white; crowded and broad.
stem_description: Tall, white; bulbous base with 2-4 concentric rings of warts; features a large, white ring.
lookalikes: Amanita caesarea (edible, orange-red but has yellow gills and stem and a large sac-like volva).
environment_tips: Look for the classic white spots (veil fragments) and the shaggy concentric rings at the stem base.

key_warnings: Contains dangerous levels of muscimol/ibotenic acid. Can cause severe poisoning and death.
cap_description: Convex to flat (5-12cm), umber to yellow-brown; covered in small, pure white, flour-like warts.
gill_description: Free, white; crowded; does not stain.
stem_description: White, with a prominent 'booted' volva forming a distinct rim around the bulb; white ring present.
lookalikes: Amanita rubescens (edible, bruises red, has dirty-grey warts).
environment_tips: Check for the 'collar' or 'rim' at the top of the bulb, a key feature of this deadly species.

habitat: Mixed forests (often near oak and pine)
key_warnings: Peach-colored cap. Contains similar toxins to A. muscaria.
cap_description: Convex (4-12cm), peach to salmon-orange, fading toward the margin; covered in yellowish warts.
gill_description: Free, white to pale cream; crowded.
stem_description: White to pale peach; bulbous base with shaggy yellow patches; features a thin ring.
lookalikes: Amanita muscaria (redder cap, white warts).
environment_tips: Specifically found in the Southeast US, typically under pine or mixed oak-pine stands.

key_warnings: "Death Cap". Contains fatal amatoxins. Responsible for the majority of fatal mushroom poisonings globally.
cap_description: Convex to flat (6-15cm), olive-green to yellowish-brown; smooth, often with a metallic sheen.
gill_description: Free, white; remain white even in age; very crowded.
stem_description: White with olive-grey scales; large white ring; base has a deep, white, sac-like volva.
smell: Sickly sweet (like rotting honey) when mature, mild when young.
lookalikes: Agaricus species (pink/brown gills, no volva), Volvopluteus gloiocephalus (pink spores, no ring).
environment_tips: EXTREME CAUTION: Always dig up the entire base to check for the sac-like volva under the soil.

key_warnings: "The Blusher". Must be cooked to destroy hemolytic toxins. Easily confused with A. pantherina.
cap_description: Convex (5-15cm), reddish-brown; covered in grey to dirty-white warts; bruises red.
gill_description: Free, white; develops reddish-brown spots where bruised or with age.
stem_description: Pinkish-white, bulbous; base and flesh turn slowly wine-red when cut or insect-damaged.
lookalikes: Amanita pantherina (highly toxic, does not bruise red, has pure white warts).
environment_tips: Look for pinkish/reddish tones in the stem base or where maggots have tunneled through the flesh.

key_warnings: Highly prized, but extreme caution required as it lacks a ring, resembling deadly species.
cap_description: Convex (5-12cm), pinkish-buff to orange-buff; margin is distinctly striate (lined); usually one large white patch.
gill_description: Free, white; crowded; soft.
stem_description: White, fragile; no ring; base features a deep, white, sac-like volva.
smell: Mild when young, fishy with age.
lookalikes: Amanita phalloides (deadly, has a ring, olive tones, non-striate margin).
environment_tips: Found under oak trees in the spring; check for the deeply lined cap margin which is characteristic.

key_warnings: Edible only when the internal flesh is pure white.
cap_description: Small (2-5cm), pear-shaped; white to tan, covered in tiny brown granules or scales.
gill_description: None; internal spore mass (gleba) is white when edible, turning olive-brown and powdery with age.
stem_description: Short, sterile base attached to the wood by white mycelial cords.
lookalikes: Scleroderma species (toxic, dark purple/black interior even when young).
environment_tips: Grows in large clusters exclusively on wood; check that the interior is solid and pure white like marshmallow.

key_warnings: Must be thoroughly cooked; can cause gastric upset in some individuals.
cap_description: Convex (3-10cm), honey-yellow to brown; covered in small, dark hair-like scales, especially at the center.
gill_description: Adnate to slightly decurrent, white becoming yellowish or pinkish-brown.
stem_description: Fibrous, brownish; features a white, persistent ring; base often fused with others in clusters.
lookalikes: Galerina marginata (deadly, grows on wood, has rusty brown spores, lacks hair-like scales).
environment_tips: Look for black, shoestring-like rhizomorphs under the bark of the host tree.

habitat: Parasitic on hardwood trees and stumps
key_warnings: "Honey Mushroom". Must be cooked thoroughly. Avoid collecting from certain toxic host trees.
cap_description: Convex (5-15cm), honey-colored to tawny; covered in tiny, dark scales that may wash off in rain.
gill_description: Adnate to decurrent, white to pale flesh-colored; may develop rusty spots in age.
stem_description: Tough, fibrous, yellowish-brown; has a thick, white, persistent ring; grows in large clusters.
lookalikes: Galerina marginata (deadly, rusty spores, smaller, fragile ring).
environment_tips: Check for white spore prints on lower caps in a cluster to distinguish from brown-spored lookalikes.

key_warnings: "Ringless Honey Mushroom". Must be cooked. Can cause gastrointestinal distress.
cap_description: Convex (3-10cm), tan to honey-brown; covered in small, dark scales.
gill_description: Decurrent, white to pinkish-tan; crowded.
stem_description: Tough, fibrous, brownish; lacks any ring; grows in dense, large clusters.
lookalikes: Omphalotus illudens (toxic, orange cap/gills, larger, non-scaly cap).
environment_tips: Grows in huge 'bouquets' from buried roots or at the base of oak trees.

key_warnings: "Crown-tipped Coral". Generally considered edible but has a peppery taste.
cap_description: Coral-like branches (4-10cm tall), white to pale tan; branch tips have a distinct cup-like crown with 3-6 points.
gill_description: None; spores produced on the surface of the branches.
stem_description: Short, tough, brownish base; branches repeatedly in a candelabra-like fashion.
lookalikes: Other coral fungi (Ramaria), but the 'crown' tips on wood are diagnostic for this species.
environment_tips: Exclusively found on decaying wood, unlike many other coral fungi which grow on soil.

key_warnings: Too tough and woody to consume. "Smoky Polypore".
cap_description: Shelf-like (2-6cm), greyish-brown to blackish; margin is usually white when actively growing.
gill_description: None; has tiny pores that are grey to black, contrasting with the paler cap.
stem_description: Absent; grows directly attached to the wood.
lookalikes: Trametes versicolor (Turkey Tail), but the grey/black pore surface is a key difference.
environment_tips: Found on stumps and logs; the 'smoky' grey pore surface is the best field identifier.

key_warnings: Too small and fragile for culinary use. "Yellow Fieldcap".
cap_description: Small (2-5cm), oval then flat; bright yellow and slimy when young, fading to greyish-white with age.
gill_description: Free, crowded; initially pale yellow, becoming rusty brown as spores mature.
stem_description: Very slender, white to pale yellow; hollow and extremely fragile.
lookalikes: None significant due to its extreme fragility and habitat on dung/grass.
environment_tips: Often found in recently mown lawns or on manure heaps; look for the bright yellow 'slime' on young caps.

key_warnings: "Porcini". Highly prized. Beware of bitter lookalikes (e.g., Tylopilus felleus).
cap_description: Large (10-30cm), convex; reddish-brown to buff, smooth and slightly tacky when moist.
gill_description: None; has tiny pores that are white when young, turning olive-yellow then greenish with age; does not stain blue.
stem_description: Thick, club-shaped; light brown with a fine, white, raised net-like pattern (reticulation) near the top.
lookalikes: Tylopilus felleus (extremely bitter, pinkish pores, dark brown reticulation).
environment_tips: Often associated with spruce or pine (conifers) and oak or beech (hardwoods).

key_warnings: Pale cap; flesh does not stain blue.
cap_description: Convex (5-15cm), exceptionally pale (whitish to buff or grey-tan); smooth, dry.
gill_description: None; has tiny pores that are white to pale yellow; slowly stains blue or greenish-blue where bruised.
stem_description: White to pale buff; lacks reticulation or is only very slightly reticulated at the very top.
lookalikes: Boletus edulis (darker cap, prominent reticulation).
environment_tips: Specifically found under oak and beech; the unusually pale 'ghost-like' appearance is diagnostic.

key_warnings: "Summer Cep". Similar to B. edulis but with a distinctly reticulated (netted) stem.
cap_description: Large (10-25cm), convex; light brown to tan; surface often cracks in dry weather to show white flesh.
gill_description: None; pores are white when young, turning yellowish-green; do not stain blue.
stem_description: Thick, bulbous; pale brown with a very prominent, raised white network covering most of the stem.
lookalikes: Boletus edulis (smoother cap, reticulation usually only at the top).
environment_tips: Found in warmer months than B. edulis, almost exclusively under hardwood trees like oak.

key_warnings: "Spring King Bolete". Fruits under snow or shortly after snowmelt.
cap_description: Large (10-25cm), convex; reddish-brown to dark chocolate brown; often with white patches from soil.
gill_description: None; pores are white and stuffed when young, turning yellowish-brown; does not stain blue.
stem_description: Massive, bulbous; white to brownish; features a white reticulation at least on the upper half.
lookalikes: Boletus edulis (fruits in autumn, cap is usually lighter).
environment_tips: Look for 'mushrumps' (bumps in the soil/needles) near melting snowbanks in high-elevation conifer forests.

key_warnings: "Yellow Stagshorn". Rubbery texture, lacks culinary value.
cap_description: Coral-like branches (3-8cm tall), bright yellow to orange; slimy/viscid when moist, rubbery when dry.
gill_description: None; spores produced on the branch surfaces.
stem_description: Tough, rooting base; branches are repeatedly forked at the tips.
lookalikes: Clavulinopsis species (grow on soil, not wood; brittle, not rubbery).
environment_tips: Exclusively found on decaying conifer wood; the rubbery, 'viscous' texture is a key identifier.

habitat: Dead wood and bark of deciduous trees
key_warnings: "Yellow Fairy Cups". Too tiny for culinary use.
cap_description: Minute (1-3mm), cup-shaped; bright lemon yellow; smooth and shiny.
gill_description: None; interior of the cup is the spore-bearing surface.
stem_description: Virtually absent; attached directly to the wood.
lookalikes: Chlorociboria aeruginascens (blue-green instead of yellow).
environment_tips: Check for mass clusters on de-barked hardwood logs in damp conditions.

key_warnings: "Mud Puppy". Massive chanterelle species. Do not confuse with toxic Jack O'Lanterns.
cap_description: Very large (up to 30cm), convex then wavy; bright orange-yellow; flesh is thick and white.
gill_description: False gills (wrinkles); decurrent, same color as the cap; blunt and forked.
stem_description: Thick, solid, yellowish; lacks a ring.
lookalikes: Omphalotus olivascens (toxic, true gills, grows on wood, flesh is orange throughout).
environment_tips: Found under Live Oak trees; often partially buried in deep leaf litter.

key_warnings: "Golden Chanterelle". False gills. Do not confuse with toxic Omphalotus species.
cap_description: Convex to funnel-shaped (3-10cm); bright egg-yellow to orange-yellow; margin is often wavy.
gill_description: False gills (ridges/veins); decurrent, shallow, and forked; same color as the cap.
stem_description: Solid, tapering downward; yellow; flesh is white and peels like string cheese.
lookalikes: Omphalotus illudens (toxic, true gills, grows in clusters on wood, smells unpleasantly).
environment_tips: Check for white flesh inside the stem; toxic lookalikes have orange flesh throughout.

key_warnings: "Cinnabar Chanterelle". Small, bright pinkish-red.
cap_description: Small (1-4cm), convex then funnel-shaped; bright flamingo-pink to cinnabar red.
gill_description: False gills; decurrent, well-spaced, and forked; same color as the cap.
stem_description: Slender, solid; reddish-pink; lacks a ring.
lookalikes: None; the bright pink-red color and false gills are unique among small woodland mushrooms.
environment_tips: Often found in mossy areas or along edges of hardwood forest paths.

key_warnings: "Dryad's Saddle". Becomes extremely tough and inedible as it matures. Smells like watermelon rind.
cap_description: Large (10-30cm), fan-shaped; yellowish-white covered in large, dark brown, feathery scales.
gill_description: None; has large, angular, white to cream-colored pores.
stem_description: Short, thick, lateral; base is usually black and velvety.
smell: Strongly of watermelon rind or cucumber.
lookalikes: None; the combination of large size, dark scales, and watermelon smell is diagnostic.
environment_tips: Check for soft, white flesh; if a knife won't cut it like butter, it's too old to eat.

key_warnings: "Iceland Moss" (A lichen). Must be boiled to remove bitter, mildly toxic acids before consumption.
cap_description: Lichen thallus (2-10cm tall), upright and shrubby; brownish-grey to olive-green with curly margins.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Flat, strap-like branches with small white spots (pseudocyphellae) on the underside.
lookalikes: None significant.
environment_tips: Found on the ground in high-altitude or arctic environments among mosses.

key_warnings: "Green Elfcup". Stains wood blue-green. Too small to eat.
cap_description: Tiny (2-5mm), cup or saucer-shaped; brilliant blue-green (teal).
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Minute, lateral or central, same color as the cup.
lookalikes: Chlorociboria aeruginosa (virtually identical, requires microscopy).
environment_tips: The mushroom is rare, but the 'blue-green' stained wood it produces is very common and easily spotted.

key_warnings: Can cause severe gastrointestinal distress.
cap_description: Large (10-20cm), convex; covered in large, brown, shaggy scales on a white background.
gill_description: Free, crowded; white, becoming brownish with age.
stem_description: Short, very thick at the base; features a prominent, movable white ring; base is 'abruptly' bulbous.
lookalikes: Macrolepiota procera (edible, tall stem with 'snakeskin' pattern).
environment_tips: Check the stem base; it should be very thick and bulbous compared to the edible Parasol.

key_warnings: "False Parasol". Causes severe gastrointestinal poisoning. Green spore print distinguishes it from edible Macrolepiota.
cap_description: Large (10-30cm), convex; white with brownish scales clustered in the center.
gill_description: Free, crowded; white when young, turning a distinct dingy green with age.
stem_description: White, staining brownish; features a large, double-edged movable ring.
lookalikes: Macrolepiota procera (edible, white/cream spore print), Chlorophyllum rhacodes (edible, white spores).
environment_tips: ALWAYS perform a spore print; if the print is green, it is this toxic species.

key_warnings: "Silverleaf Fungus". Tough and leathery.
cap_description: Shelf-like or crust-like (1-3cm); fuzzy/hairy grey upper surface with a wavy margin.
gill_description: None; underside is smooth and brilliant purple when fresh, fading to brown.
stem_description: Absent; attached directly to the wood.
lookalikes: Stereum species (underrside is yellow or brown, never purple).
environment_tips: Causes 'Silverleaf disease' in living fruit trees; look for the characteristic purple underside.

key_warnings: A lichen ("Cup Lichen"). No culinary value.
cap_description: Lichen thallus (1-2cm tall); slender green stalks ending in a perfectly flared cup.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: The entire structure is covered in a fine, floury green powder (soredia).
lookalikes: Other Cladonia species (some have red tips or different cup shapes).
environment_tips: Commonly found on old, mossy stumps in shady forests.

key_warnings: "Reindeer Lichen". Must be boiled heavily to remove acidic compounds.
cap_description: Lichen thallus (5-10cm tall), shrubby; ash-grey to white; highly branched with tips pointing in one direction.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Hollow, cylindrical branches; texture is somewhat brittle when dry, spongey when wet.
lookalikes: Cladonia stellaris (more dome-shaped clusters, yellowish-green tint).
environment_tips: Forms large, greyish 'carpets' on the forest floor in northern regions.

key_warnings: "Star Reindeer Lichen". Generally not consumed by humans.
cap_description: Lichen thallus (5-10cm tall); forms distinct, rounded, cauliflower-like domes; yellowish-green color.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Very densely branched; lacks a main 'trunk'.
lookalikes: Cladonia rangiferina (ash-grey, not dome-shaped).
environment_tips: Look for the very neat, rounded 'pompom' growth form on the ground.

key_warnings: "Clouded Agaric". Contains nebuline; causes severe gastric upset in many individuals. Avoid.
cap_description: Large (10-20cm), convex then flat or depressed; clouded grey to brownish-grey; margin remains inrolled.
gill_description: Decurrent, crowded; white to pale cream; easily separable from the cap flesh.
stem_description: Thick, club-shaped; greyish-white; fibrous and solid.
smell: Strong and unpleasant; sweetish but sickly, often compared to coal gas.
lookalikes: Entoloma sinuatum (toxic, pink spores, non-decurrent gills).
environment_tips: Often grows in large 'fairy rings' in leaf litter or pine needles.

key_warnings: Also known as Lepista nuda (Blewit). Must be cooked. Beware of toxic Cortinarius lookalikes that have rusty-brown spores.
cap_description: Medium (6-15cm), convex then flat; brilliant violet to purple when young, fading to brownish-lilac with age.
gill_description: Adnexed to slightly decurrent, crowded; violet-purple, eventually turning buff-brown.
stem_description: Thick, fibrous, violet to greyish-lilac; base is often swollen and covered in violet-tinted mycelium.
smell: Strong and distinctive; floral, fruity, or like frozen orange juice.
lookalikes: Cortinarius species (toxic, have a web-like cortina and rusty brown spore prints).
environment_tips: Often found in 'fairy rings' in garden mulch or thick leaf litter; always check for a white/pinkish spore print.

habitat: Sandy soils, often along forest paths
key_warnings: Too tough and leathery for consumption.
cap_description: Small to medium (2-10cm), funnel-shaped; velvety, with concentric zones of cinnamon, brown, and grey.
gill_description: None; underside is covered in tiny, brownish-grey pores that are decurrent.
stem_description: Central, tough, velvety, and brownish-rust colored.
lookalikes: Phaeolus schweinitzii (larger, grows at the base of trees, stains black with KOH).
environment_tips: Commonly found on sandy, nutrient-poor soil along the edges of forest trails.

key_warnings: "Fairy Inkcap". Too small and fragile for culinary use.
cap_description: Tiny (0.5-1.5cm), bell-shaped; pleated/grooved; initially white to pale buff, turning greyish.
gill_description: Adnate, crowded; white then grey, finally black but does not dissolve into ink.
stem_description: Slender, white, translucent, and very fragile.
lookalikes: Other small Mycena species, but the dense clusters on wood are characteristic.
environment_tips: Grows in massive, spectacular 'armies' of hundreds of individuals on or around old stumps.

key_warnings: "Mica Cap". Auto-digests (turns to black ink) shortly after picking. Must be cooked immediately.
cap_description: Small (2-5cm), bell-shaped; tawny-brown with distinct grooves; covered in tiny, glistening mica-like granules when young.
gill_description: Adnexed, crowded; white, becoming purple-brown then black and dissolving into ink.
stem_description: Slender, white, hollow, and fragile.
lookalikes: Coprinopsis atramentaria (larger, lacks glistening granules, toxic with alcohol).
environment_tips: Look for the glistening 'mica' particles on the cap, though they can wash off in rain.

key_warnings: "Common Inkcap". Contains coprine. Causes severe, heart-racing illness if alcohol is consumed within a few days of eating.
cap_description: Medium (3-7cm), egg-shaped then bell-shaped; grey to brownish-grey; surface is smooth or slightly scaly.
gill_description: Free, crowded; white then grey, eventually black and dissolving into liquid ink.
stem_description: White, hollow; features a very faint, narrow ring-like zone near the base.
lookalikes: Coprinus comatus (larger, much more shaggy, non-toxic with alcohol).
environment_tips: Often fruits in large clusters near buried wood or old stumps in parks and gardens.

key_warnings: "Hare's Foot Inkcap". Auto-digests extremely rapidly; flesh is virtually non-existent.
cap_description: Small (2-4cm), initially cylindrical then bell-shaped; covered in dense white, woolly hairs when young.
gill_description: Free, crowded; white, rapidly turning black and dissolving.
stem_description: Very slender, white, and covered in delicate white hairs (flocculose).
lookalikes: Coprinopsis nivea (grows on dung, much whiter and more mealy).
environment_tips: Fruits and disappears within a few hours, usually early in the morning after rain.

key_warnings: "Shaggy Mane". Must be picked before gills turn pink/black and cooked immediately before auto-digestion.
cap_description: Large (5-15cm tall), cylindrical; covered in large, shaggy white scales; margin turns pink then black and curls up.
gill_description: Free, crowded; white, then pink, then black and dissolving into ink.
stem_description: Tall, white, hollow; features a movable white ring.
lookalikes: Coprinopsis atramentaria (grey, not shaggy, toxic with alcohol).
environment_tips: Look for them in freshly disturbed soil or parks; the tall, shaggy 'lawyer's wig' look is unmistakable.

key_warnings: "White-egg Bird's Nest Fungus". Much too small for culinary use.
cap_description: Minute (5-10mm), cup-shaped; yellow to tan; initially covered by a thin yellow membrane.
gill_description: None; contains small, white, lens-shaped 'eggs' (peridioles) inside the cup.
stem_description: Absent; attached directly to the substrate.
lookalikes: Cyathus striatus (greyish, with distinct grooves inside the cup).
environment_tips: Often found in garden mulch or on decaying twigs in moist, shaded areas.

key_warnings: "Veiled Polypore". Tough, leathery texture.
cap_description: Small (2-5cm), globe-shaped to hoof-shaped; creamy white to tan; has a unique 'veil' membrane covering the pores.
gill_description: None; pores are hidden inside a chamber formed by the outer membrane.
stem_description: Absent; attached directly to the bark of conifers.
lookalikes: None; the unique 'pocket' or 'veil' covering the pores is diagnostic.
environment_tips: Almost always found on recently dead conifers, often after forest fires; look for the small hole in the 'veil' where insects enter.

key_warnings: "Thin-maze Flat Polypore". Tough, woody, and corky.
cap_description: Shelf-like (5-15cm), semi-circular; greyish-brown to reddish-brown; often zonate with a sharp margin.
gill_description: None; underside features maze-like or elongated pores that turn reddish-brown when bruised.
stem_description: Absent.
lookalikes: Daedaleopsis tricolor (underrside is much more gill-like and cap is darker red).
environment_tips: Common on dead willow and birch branches; the reddish bruising of the pore surface is a key field test.

key_warnings: Very tough and woody texture.
cap_description: Shelf-like (3-10cm); dark reddish-brown to blackish; surface is often zonated and slightly hairy.
gill_description: None; the pore surface is remarkably gill-like (lamellate), radiating from the base.
stem_description: Absent.
lookalikes: Daedaleopsis confragosa (underrside has maze-like pores rather than gills).
environment_tips: Look for the strikingly regular 'gills' on a polypore growing from hardwood branches.

key_warnings: "Shrimp of the Woods". The "aborted" lumpy form is edible. Avoid the normal gilled form due to toxic lookalikes.
cap_description: Aborted form: Lumpy, white, irregular masses (2-10cm). Gilled form: Grey-brown, convex cap (5-10cm).
gill_description: Gilled form: Decurrent, white becoming pinkish. Aborted form: None.
stem_description: Gilled form: Grey-brown, fibrous. Aborted form: Indistinct.
lookalikes: Normal gilled form looks like toxic Entoloma sinuatum. Only the 'white popcorn' lumps are safe.
environment_tips: Always found in the presence of Honey Mushrooms (Armillaria), which this fungus parasitizes.

key_warnings: "Boreal Oakmoss". A lichen with no culinary value.
cap_description: Lichen thallus (3-10cm), shrubby and pendant; yellowish-green to grey-green.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Branches are irregular, somewhat flattened, and covered in tiny, grainy spots (soredia).
lookalikes: Evernia prunastri (flatter branches, paler underside).
environment_tips: Commonly hangs from the branches of spruce and fir trees in boreal forests.

key_warnings: "Oakmoss". Used heavily in perfumery, but not for human consumption.
cap_description: Lichen thallus (3-8cm), pendant; strap-like branches that are grey-green on top and white underneath.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Soft and pliable when wet, brittle when dry.
smell: Strongly earthy and 'mossy' when processed; used as a base note in perfumes.
lookalikes: Ramalina species (same color on both sides of the branches).
environment_tips: Look for the distinct color contrast between the top and bottom of the flattened branches.

key_warnings: Wild "Enoki". Fruits in freezing weather. Extreme caution: Strongly resembles the deadly Galerina marginata.
cap_description: Small (2-7cm), convex; bright orange-brown to tawny; very slimy/viscid when moist.
gill_description: Adnexed, white to pale yellow; crowded.
stem_description: Tough, dark brown to black and velvety, especially at the base; lacks a ring.
lookalikes: Galerina marginata (deadly, has a ring, brown spores, non-velvety stem).
environment_tips: DANGER: Always check for a white spore print and a velvety stem; if it has brown spores, it is deadly.

key_warnings: "Tinder Fungus". Historically used for fire-starting and wound dressing. Far too woody to eat.
cap_description: Large (10-40cm), hoof-shaped; grey to silver-grey with distinct hard, concentric ridges.
gill_description: None; has tiny, brownish pores on the underside.
stem_description: Absent; grows directly as a bracket from the tree trunk.
lookalikes: Phellinus igniarius (darker, more cracked surface, grows on willow).
environment_tips: Extremely hard; cannot be crushed by hand. Look for the 'horse-hoof' shape on dead birch.

key_warnings: "Birch Polypore". Very tough and bitter. Used in traditional medicinal teas.
cap_description: Shelf-like (5-20cm), smooth, brownish-grey; margin is thick and rounded, often curving over the pore surface.
gill_description: None; pores are white to cream, becoming brownish with age.
stem_description: Absent or a very short, lateral nub.
lookalikes: None; the smooth, 'kidney-shaped' brown bracket on birch is unique.
environment_tips: Found exclusively on birch trees; the flesh is white, corky, and very bitter if tasted.

key_warnings: Tough, woody polypore.
cap_description: Shelf-like (10-30cm); upper surface is greyish with a brilliant red or orange 'varnished' margin when fresh.
gill_description: None; pore surface is white to pale yellow; does not stain.
stem_description: Absent.
smell: Strong and unpleasant, like fermenting fruit or old gym socks.
lookalikes: Fomitopsis pinicola (European equivalent; requires chemical tests to distinguish).
environment_tips: Look for the striking 'red belt' near the margin of the cap on dead conifer logs.

key_warnings: "Red-belted Conk". Extremely tough and woody.
cap_description: Shelf-like (10-40cm), hoof-shaped; greyish-black with a distinct, orange-red band near the white margin.
gill_description: None; has tiny, cream-colored pores that exude clear droplets when young.
stem_description: Absent.
lookalikes: Ganoderma applanatum (pores stain brown when scratched, no red belt).
environment_tips: Very common on dead conifers; the hard, resinous surface will melt if a match is held to it.

key_warnings: "Deadly Skullcap". Contains fatal amatoxins (same as Death Cap). Severe liver damage. Do not touch or ingest.
cap_description: Small (1-4cm), convex to flat; honey-brown to tawny, fading as it dries (hygrophanous).
gill_description: Adnate to decurrent, crowded; yellow-brown, becoming rusty-brown as spores mature.
stem_description: Slender, brownish; features a small, fragile, brownish ring; base is often covered in white fibrils.
lookalikes: Flammulina velutipes (edible, white spores, no ring), Armillaria species (white spores, larger).
environment_tips: DEADLY: Always perform a spore print for small brown mushrooms on wood; rusty-brown = DANGER.

key_warnings: "Artist's Conk". White pore surface bruises brown when scratched. Far too woody to eat.
cap_description: Large (10-50cm), shelf-like and flat; greyish-brown to cinnamon-brown, often covered in a dusting of brown spores.
gill_description: None; underside has tiny white pores that stain dark brown instantly when scratched.
stem_description: Absent; attached broadly to the tree trunk.
lookalikes: Fomitopsis pinicola (pores do not stain brown, has a red belt).
environment_tips: Used by artists for 'drawing' on the pore surface; found on dead or dying hardwoods like beech and maple.

key_warnings: A North American Reishi relative. Tough and corky; used for teas/extracts.
cap_description: Medium (5-15cm), fan-shaped; yellowish to reddish-brown, covered in a shiny, varnish-like crust.
gill_description: None; tiny white pores that turn brownish with age.
stem_description: Usually present, lateral, long, and brownish; also features a shiny, varnished surface.
lookalikes: Ganoderma lucidum (European Reishi; G. curtisii is more common in the eastern US).
environment_tips: Check for the 'varnished' look on both the cap and the stem; grows near the base of oak trees.

key_warnings: Western Reishi relative. Large, tough, and varnished-looking.
cap_description: Large (10-40cm), fan-shaped; brilliant reddish-brown to mahogany with a high-gloss, varnished finish.
gill_description: None; underside is white when fresh, staining brown where handled.
stem_description: Absent or a short, thick, lateral nub; also varnished.
lookalikes: Ganoderma tsugae (grows on hemlock, smaller).
environment_tips: Look for massive, glossy red-brown brackets on dead fir or spruce in the Pacific Northwest.

key_warnings: "Hemlock Varnish Shelf". Tough and corky; traditionally used for teas.
cap_description: Medium to large (5-30cm), fan-shaped; bright red-orange to mahogany with a shiny, varnished surface.
gill_description: None; tiny pores are white, becoming brownish with age.
stem_description: Lateral, short, and varnished; same color as the cap.
lookalikes: Ganoderma lucidum (grows on hardwood, not hemlock).
environment_tips: Exclusively found on hemlock trees (Tsuga); the white flesh distinguishes it from some other Ganoderma species.

key_warnings: "Parrot Waxcap". Extremely slimy and small. Edibility is debated; best avoided.
cap_description: Small (1-4cm), bell-shaped; bright green when young, fading to yellow, orange, or even pinkish.
gill_description: Adnate, thick and distant; yellow-green to orange-yellow.
stem_description: Slender, green (especially at the top), and extremely slimy/viscid.
lookalikes: None; the bright green color and intense sliminess are unique.
environment_tips: Found in old, nutrient-poor grasslands; the 'parrot-like' variety of colors in one patch is characteristic.

key_warnings: "Rusty Gilled Polypore". Tough, corky, and causes brown rot in wood.
cap_description: Small (2-8cm), shelf-like; fuzzy/hairy when young; bright orange-brown margin with a darker brown center.
gill_description: None; however, the pore surface consists of very elongated, gill-like structures that are brownish.
stem_description: Absent.
lookalikes: Trametes species (underrside has true pores, not gill-like structures).
environment_tips: Commonly found on sun-exposed conifer logs, fence posts, and even railroad ties.

key_warnings: "Secret Writing Lichen". Looks like scribbles on bark. No culinary value.
cap_description: Lichen thallus; forms thin, greyish-white crusty patches on tree bark.
gill_description: None; produces black, elongated, often branched 'writing' marks (lirellae) on the surface.
stem_description: Absent.
lookalikes: Other 'Script' lichens (require chemical tests or microscopy to distinguish).
environment_tips: Look for the appearance of black 'hieroglyphs' or 'Morse code' on smooth bark like beech or hazel.

key_warnings: "Maitake" or "Hen of the Woods". Highly prized edible and medicinal mushroom.
cap_description: Large cluster (20-60cm across) of many overlapping, fan-shaped caps; grey-brown to olive-brown.
gill_description: None; underside has tiny white pores that are decurrent onto the stems.
stem_description: Many-branched from a single, thick, white base; branches are short and white.
lookalikes: Meripilus sumstinei (Black-staining Polypore; caps stain black when bruised).
environment_tips: Check for clusters at the very base of old oak trees; the many 'ruffled' caps give it a 'hen-like' appearance.

key_warnings: Contains psilocybin/psilocin. Extremely bitter taste.
cap_description: Small to medium (2-8cm), convex; covered in reddish-purple to reddish-brown scales on a yellow background.
gill_description: Adnexed, crowded; bright yellow, becoming rusty-orange as spores mature.
stem_description: Yellowish, often with a slight purple tint at the base; features a delicate, soon-disappearing ring.
lookalikes: Tricholomopsis rutilans (non-bitter, white spores, lacks rusty gills).
environment_tips: Check for blue-green staining at the base of the stem or on the cap (though often faint); the taste is extremely bitter.

key_warnings: "False Morel". Contains highly toxic gyromitrin (rocket fuel chemical). Can be fatal; even inhaling cooking fumes is dangerous.
cap_description: Medium (4-10cm), brain-like and wrinkled; reddish-brown to dark brown; lacks a clear internal chamber.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Thick, whitish to tan, and chambered or folded inside; the cap is attached only at the top of the stem.
lookalikes: True Morels (Morchella; cap is pitted like a honeycomb, not brain-like; cap is attached to the stem at the base).
environment_tips: DANGER: Never consume. If testing, cut vertically to see if the cap is brain-like and the stem is solid/chambered.

habitat: Conifer and mixed forests, near melting snow
key_warnings: "Snow Morel". Contains gyromitrin toxins.
cap_description: Large (5-15cm), brain-like and heavily convoluted; yellowish-brown to tan; thick and heavy.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Short, very thick, and whitish; often nearly as wide as the cap.
lookalikes: Gyromitra esculenta (darker reddish-brown cap, more slender stem).
environment_tips: Found in high-elevation forests in early spring, often right at the edge of snowbanks.

key_warnings: "Saddle-shaped False Morel". Contains gyromitrin toxins. Highly dangerous to consume raw.
cap_description: Medium (4-10cm); saddle-shaped with 2-3 lobes; reddish-brown to dark brown; surface is smooth or slightly wavy.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Thin, hollow, whitish to brownish, and often slightly flattened.
lookalikes: Helvella species (smaller, stem is often deeply fluted/grooved).
environment_tips: Fruits in autumn rather than spring, typically found on well-rotted conifer wood or woodchips.

key_warnings: "Coral Tooth". Excellent edible when young and white.
cap_description: Large cluster (10-30cm), many-branched; covered in many short, white, icicle-like 'teeth' or spines (0.5-1cm long).
gill_description: None; spores produced on the downward-pointing spines.
stem_description: Main branches arise from a single, tough base attached to the log.
lookalikes: Hericium americanum (spines are much longer, in 'pompom' clusters).
environment_tips: Look for brilliant white 'ice-sculptures' on decaying hardwood; avoid if they have turned yellowish or brown.

habitat: Wounds of living hardwoods or dead logs
key_warnings: "Lion's Mane". Prized edible with a seafood-like texture.
cap_description: Large, unbranched, rounded mass (10-25cm); covered in long (1-5cm), white, icicle-like spines.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Tough, solid base attached directly to the tree wound or log.
lookalikes: None; the unbranched, shaggy white mass is unique.
environment_tips: Often grows high up in the wounds of living oak or beech trees; can be seen from a distance.

key_warnings: "False Chanterelle". Has caused gastrointestinal upset and hallucinations in some individuals. Avoid.
cap_description: Small (2-6cm), convex then funnel-shaped; bright orange to yellow-orange; surface is slightly fuzzy.
gill_description: Decurrent, thin, and repeatedly forked; brilliant orange; easily separable from the cap flesh.
stem_description: Slender, same color as cap or slightly darker brown at the base; hollow.
lookalikes: Cantharellus cibarius (Choice edible, false gills/ridges, white flesh inside, smells of apricots).
environment_tips: Check the gills; if they are true, thin, forked gills and the flesh is orange, it is the False Chanterelle.

key_warnings: "Sulfur Tuft". Extremely bitter taste. Causes severe gastrointestinal distress, nausea, and vomiting.
cap_description: Small (2-6cm), convex; bright sulfur-yellow with an orange-brown center.
gill_description: Adnate, crowded; sulfur-yellow, becoming a distinct greenish-grey as spores mature.
stem_description: Slender, yellowish, often with a faint greenish tint; grows in large, dense clusters.
lookalikes: Hypholoma lateritium (edible, brick-red cap, no greenish gills).
environment_tips: DANGER: Always check for the greenish-grey gill color; the taste is instantly and overwhelmingly bitter.

key_warnings: "Brick Cap". Must be cooked thoroughly. Bitter if eaten raw.
cap_description: Medium (3-10cm), convex; distinct brick-red to reddish-brown with a paler, yellowish margin.
gill_description: Adnate, crowded; whitish-grey, becoming purple-grey as spores mature (never green).
stem_description: Whitish to brownish; often has white veil fragments on the cap margin when young.
lookalikes: Hypholoma fasciculare (toxic, bright yellow cap, greenish gills, extremely bitter).
environment_tips: Look for large clusters on hardwood stumps in late autumn; the brick-red cap is the best identifier.

key_warnings: "Monk's Hood Lichen". No culinary value.
cap_description: Lichen thallus; forms leafy (foliose) grey-green rosettes; lobes are puffy and hollow inside.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Absent; underside is black and wrinkled.
lookalikes: Parmelia sulcata (lobes are not puffy or hollow).
environment_tips: One of the most common lichens; the 'puffy' hollow lobes that look like inflated pillows are diagnostic.

habitat: Parasitic on Russula and Lactarius species
key_warnings: "Lobster Mushroom". Firm texture and seafood-like aroma.
cap_description: Not a true mushroom, but a parasitic crust; brilliant orange to reddish-orange; surface is covered in tiny bumps.
gill_description: None; the parasite covers the gills of the host, making them look like shallow, blunt ridges.
stem_description: The entire host mushroom is covered in the orange crust, becoming very firm and heavy.
smell: Distinctly seafood-like (like cooked lobster or shrimp).
lookalikes: None; the brilliant orange, sandpaper-like surface on a deformed mushroom is unmistakable.
environment_tips: Found where the host mushrooms (Russula brevipes or Lactarius) grow; often partially buried in soil.

key_warnings: "Bay Bolete". Pores stain blue-green when bruised. Excellent edible.
cap_description: Medium (5-15cm), convex; dark bay-brown to chestnut brown; smooth and slightly sticky when wet.
gill_description: None; tiny pores are pale yellow, staining blue-green immediately when pressed.
stem_description: Slender to slightly club-shaped, brownish; lacks any net-like pattern (reticulation).
lookalikes: Boletus edulis (pores don't stain blue, has reticulated stem).
environment_tips: Look for them in conifer needles or moss; the immediate blue-green pore staining is the key test.

key_warnings: "Chaga". Very hard, black, and crusty on the outside; must be processed into extracts or teas.
cap_description: None; forms a sterile, clumpy growth (conk) that looks like burnt charcoal (10-40cm).
gill_description: None; the actual spore-bearing surface is hidden under the bark and rarely seen.
stem_description: Absent; grows as an irregular protrusion from the trunk of birch trees.
lookalikes: Tree burls (which are part of the wood and not a fungus).
environment_tips: Look for the golden-orange internal color when a small piece is chipped off the black 'charred' exterior.

key_warnings: "Resinous Polypore". Edible only when very young and soft; becomes extremely tough with age.
cap_description: Shelf-like (5-20cm), velvety and dark reddish-brown; exuded clear to amber resin droplets when young.
gill_description: None; pores are white, turning brownish when bruised or with age.
stem_description: Absent.
lookalikes: Ischnoderma benzoinum (grows on conifers, otherwise very similar).
environment_tips: Look for the 'sweating' amber droplets on the white margin in early autumn; the flesh is soft and juicy when edible.

key_warnings: "Wood Tuft". Extreme Caution: Can easily be confused with the deadly Galerina marginata which grows in the same habitat.
cap_description: Small (2-6cm), convex; two-toned (hygrophanous) brown, drying from the center to a pale tan while the edge remains dark.
gill_description: Adnate to decurrent, crowded; pale brown, becoming cinnamon-brown as spores mature.
stem_description: Slender, brownish; features a small ring; below the ring, the stem is covered in distinct, recurved brownish scales.
lookalikes: Galerina marginata (deadly, stem is fibrous/silky, not scaly below the ring).
environment_tips: EXTREME DANGER: The scaly stem below the ring is the primary identifier to distinguish it from the deadly Galerina.

key_warnings: "Purple-gilled Laccaria". Edible, but closely resembles toxic Cortinarius species. Check for white spore print.
cap_description: Medium (5-15cm), convex then flat; light brownish to greyish-tan; surface is smooth and often cracks.
gill_description: Adnate to decurrent, very thick and distant; brilliant deep purple when fresh.
stem_description: Tall, thick, and very fibrous; same color as the cap.
lookalikes: Cortinarius species (toxic, have a cobweb-like veil and rusty brown spores).
environment_tips: Always confirm a white spore print; the brilliant purple gills and very tough, fibrous stem are diagnostic.

key_warnings: "Saffron Milk Cap". Exudes bright orange latex when cut that eventually stains green.
cap_description: Medium (5-15cm), funnel-shaped; orange with concentric darker orange zones; stains green where bruised.
gill_description: Decurrent, crowded; bright orange, staining green with age or handling.
stem_description: White to orange, often with darker orange 'pits' (scrobiculae) on the surface; exuded orange milk.
lookalikes: Lactarius deterrimus (grows under spruce, also edible but less prized).
environment_tips: Exclusively found under pine trees; the combination of orange milk and green staining is unique and safe.

key_warnings: "Woolly Milkcap". Extremely spicy/acrid raw. Causes severe gastrointestinal distress unless repeatedly boiled (a common practice in Eastern Europe).
cap_description: Medium (5-12cm), funnel-shaped; pinkish-buff with concentric zones; margin is very hairy/woolly.
gill_description: Decurrent, crowded; pale pinkish-white; exuded white, unchanging milk.
stem_description: White to pale pink, often with orange-buff pits; hollow.
lookalikes: Lactarius pubescens (paler, lacks concentric zones, also associated with birch).
environment_tips: Almost always found under birch trees; the 'shaggy' or 'woolly' cap margin is the most striking feature.

habitat: Damp woods, often near birch or spruce
key_warnings: "Ugly Milkcap". Contains necatorin, a highly mutagenic compound. Do not consume.
cap_description: Large (8-20cm), funnel-shaped; dark olive-brown to almost black; slimy when moist.
gill_description: Decurrent, crowded; pale yellow, staining dark brown where bruised; exuded white milk.
stem_description: Short, thick, and same color as the cap (olive-brown).
lookalikes: None; its 'ugly' dark olive-green to blackish appearance is quite unique.
environment_tips: Common in wet, mossy areas under birch; historically eaten in some regions, but now known to be mutagenic.

key_warnings: "Chicken of the Woods". Can cause gastric upset in some people, especially if growing on conifers or eucalyptus.
cap_description: Large overlapping clusters of fan-shaped caps (10-50cm across); brilliant sulfur-yellow to bright orange.
gill_description: None; underside has tiny, brilliant sulfur-yellow pores.
stem_description: Absent; attached directly to the wood.
lookalikes: Laetiporus gilbertsonii (grows on eucalyptus, higher risk of toxicity).
environment_tips: The bright orange color fades to white as it ages; only the tender outer edges should be harvested.

habitat: Associated with poplar and aspen trees
key_warnings: Must be thoroughly cooked to avoid gastric upset. Flesh slowly darkens when cut.
cap_description: Large (8-20cm), convex; bright orange to orange-red; smooth and slightly felt-like.
gill_description: None; pores are white to greyish-white, becoming slightly brownish with age.
stem_description: Tall, thick, and covered in white scales (scabers) that do not turn black (unlike many other Leccinums).
lookalikes: Leccinum aurantiacum (stem scales turn reddish-brown then black).
environment_tips: Exclusively found under aspen or poplar; the white stem scales on an orange-capped bolete are diagnostic.

key_warnings: "Red-capped Scaber Stalk". Must be cooked thoroughly (15+ minutes) to neutralize toxins.
cap_description: Large (8-25cm), convex; brilliant orange-red to reddish-brown; smooth.
gill_description: None; pores are white, becoming greyish; does not stain blue.
stem_description: White, covered in small scales (scabers) that are initially white then turn reddish-brown or black.
lookalikes: Leccinum scabrum (brown cap, associated with birch).
environment_tips: Flesh turns purple-grey then black when cut; this is normal for this species but requires thorough cooking.

key_warnings: "Birch Bolete". Flesh becomes extremely mushy when cooked.
cap_description: Medium to large (5-15cm), convex; light brown to grey-brown; surface is smooth and dry.
gill_description: None; pores are white, turning brownish-grey; very deep and easily separable from the cap.
stem_description: Tall, slender, white; covered in dense, small black scales (scabers).
lookalikes: None; the brown cap and black-scaled stem under birch are classic markers.
environment_tips: Always associated with birch; the stem is very tough and fibrous, while the cap is soft.

key_warnings: "Orange Birch Bolete". Must be cooked thoroughly to avoid severe gastrointestinal distress.
cap_description: Large (10-25cm), convex; bright orange to orange-yellow; margin often has overlapping skin fragments.
gill_description: None; pores are greyish-white, becoming darker grey with age.
stem_description: Tall, thick, and white; covered in prominent black scales (scabers).
lookalikes: Leccinum aurantiacum (grows under aspen, has reddish-brown stem scales).
environment_tips: Found under birch; flesh turns wine-red then blackish when cut; ensure thorough cooking to neutralize toxins.

key_warnings: "Wood Blewit". Synonym for Clitocybe nuda. Never eat raw.
cap_description: Medium (6-15cm), convex; lilac to violet, fading to buff; flesh is also lilac.
gill_description: Adnexed, crowded; violet-purple, eventually turning brownish.
stem_description: Thick, violet, fibrous; lacks a ring.
smell: Fruity or floral, similar to frozen orange juice.
lookalikes: Toxic violet Cortinarius (have rusty spores and a cobweb-like veil).
environment_tips: Check for white to pale pink spore print; Cortinarius will have rusty-brown spore print.

key_warnings: "Redlead Roundhead". Mildly toxic; avoid. Common in landscaped urban areas.
cap_description: Small (2-6cm), convex; brilliant scarlet-red to orange-red, often with white veil fragments on the margin.
gill_description: Adnate, crowded; pale greyish, becoming dark purple-grey or black as spores mature.
stem_description: White to yellowish-tan, often with reddish stains; features a faint ring-like zone.
lookalikes: None; the brilliant red cap in woodchips is a very distinctive urban identifier.
environment_tips: Look for the white 'pustules' or veil fragments around the edge of the bright red cap.

key_warnings: "Reddening Lepiota". Entire mushroom bruises and ages to a reddish-brown color.
cap_description: Large (10-20cm), convex; covered in large reddish-brown scales on a white background; center is solid dark brown.
gill_description: Free, crowded; white, but turns reddish-orange when bruised.
stem_description: Thick, often club-shaped or swollen; white, but stains bright yellow then red when handled.
lookalikes: Chlorophyllum molybdites (toxic, green spores, does not stain red).
environment_tips: Check for the yellow-then-red color change when the stem is scratched; often grows in dense clusters.

key_warnings: "White Dapperling". High Risk: Visually identical to deadly Amanita species (like the Destroying Angel), though it lacks a volva.
cap_description: Medium (5-12cm), convex; pure white to ivory, smooth and slightly silky.
gill_description: Free, crowded; white, but turns a faint pinkish color in old specimens.
stem_description: Tall, white, hollow; features a white, movable ring; base is slightly swollen but lacks a sac (volva).
lookalikes: Deadly Amanita bisporigera (Destroying Angel; has a sac-like volva at the base).
environment_tips: EXTREME DANGER: Always dig up the entire base to confirm the ABSENCE of a volva; avoid if unsure.

habitat: Bark of deciduous trees in old-growth forests
key_warnings: "Lungwort". An indicator of good air quality; not a culinary mushroom.
cap_description: Lichen thallus; large, leafy (foliose) and green when wet, grey when dry; surface is deeply pitted and ridged.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Attached broadly to the bark; underside is pale and fuzzy (tomentose) with white spots.
lookalikes: None; the resemblance to human lung tissue is very striking.
environment_tips: Only found in clean, unpolluted old-growth forests; look for it on the trunks of maple and oak.

key_warnings: "Wolf's Milk". Actually an amoeba colony (slime mold), not a true fungus.
cap_description: Minute (3-15mm), globe-shaped; initially bright pink or orange, maturing to grey or brownish-black.
gill_description: None; interior is filled with a pinkish 'milk' when young, turning into grey powder (spores).
stem_description: Absent; grows as small, scattered or clustered dots on logs.
lookalikes: Immature puffballs (but Lycogala is much smaller and has pink 'milk').
environment_tips: Common on well-rotted logs; poke a young pink specimen to see the 'wolf's milk' exude.

key_warnings: "Common Puffball". Edible only when the interior is completely pure white and firm.
cap_description: Small to medium (3-8cm), pear-shaped; white to cream; covered in short, cone-shaped warts that leave scars when rubbed off.
gill_description: None; internal spore mass (gleba) is pure white when young, turning olive-brown and powdery with age.
stem_description: Indistinct; a sterile, tapering base that is also white and firm when young.
lookalikes: Amanita eggs (DANGER: cutting in half reveals a developing mushroom inside; puffballs are solid white).
environment_tips: Check that the interior is as white and solid as cream cheese; if it is yellow, green, or brown, it is inedible.

key_warnings: "Pear-shaped Puffball". Synonym for Apioperdon pyriforme. Edible only when the interior is pure white.
cap_description: Small (2-5cm), pear-shaped; tan to brownish; surface is smooth or covered in very fine granules.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Tapering, sterile base attached to wood by white mycelial strands (rhizomorphs).
lookalikes: Scleroderma species (toxic, dark interior when young).
environment_tips: Grows in large, dense clusters exclusively on wood, unlike the Common Puffball which grows on soil.

key_warnings: "Parasol Mushroom". Tall with a snakeskin-patterned stem. Beware of toxic Chlorophyllum lookalikes.
cap_description: Large (10-30cm), convex then flat with a central bump (umbo); white with large, shaggy brown scales.
gill_description: Free, very crowded; white, but may turn creamy-pinkish with age.
stem_description: Very tall (15-40cm), slender; features a distinct brownish 'snakeskin' pattern and a large, movable double ring.
lookalikes: Chlorophyllum molybdites (toxic, green spores, lacks snakeskin stem pattern).
environment_tips: Check the stem for the 'snakeskin' pattern; if the stem is smooth and the spores are green, it is toxic.

key_warnings: "Trembling Merulius". Gelatinous, wrinkled crust fungus; no culinary value.
cap_description: Crust-like or slightly shelf-like (2-5cm); white and fuzzy on top with a wavy, often translucent margin.
gill_description: None; the underside is bright orange to reddish-brown and covered in shallow, translucent wrinkles/pores.
stem_description: Absent; grows flat against the wood.
lookalikes: Phlebia radiata (more brilliantly orange and wrinkled).
environment_tips: Found on the underside of wet hardwood logs; the 'trembling' gelatinous texture is characteristic.

key_warnings: "Red Stinkhorn". Emits a foul, rotting-meat odor to attract flies.
cap_description: None; the 'head' of the stalk is covered in a dark olive-green, slimy, foul-smelling spore mass (gleba).
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Slender, spongy stalk (5-10cm); bright pink to red; the tip is pointed and the gleba is restricted to the upper part.
smell: Extremely foul, like rotting meat or carrion.
lookalikes: Mutinus caninus (paler orange stalk, head is less distinct).
environment_tips: Often found in urban mulch; look for the bright pink 'fingers' emerging from white 'eggs' in the soil.

key_warnings: "Bleeding Fairy Helmet". Exudes a dark red, blood-like latex when the stem is snapped. Too small to eat.
cap_description: Small (1-4cm), bell-shaped; reddish-brown to pinkish-grey; margin is finely scalloped or fringed.
gill_description: Adnate, distant; whitish to pale pinkish-brown.
stem_description: Slender, hollow, same color as the cap; snaps easily to release a dark burgundy 'blood'.
lookalikes: Other Mycena species, but the dark red 'bleeding' latex is unique.
environment_tips: Grows in small clusters on well-rotted logs; the bleeding stem is the definitive field test.

key_warnings: "Orange Mycena". Bright orange and slimy.
cap_description: Small (1-4cm), bell-shaped; brilliant orange; very slimy/viscid when moist; color fades slightly with age.
gill_description: Adnate, crowded; bright orange with a darker orange edge (cheilocystidia).
stem_description: Slender, orange, and extremely slimy; often found in large, dense clusters.
lookalikes: None; the brilliant orange color and intense sliminess on hardwood are very distinctive.
environment_tips: Look for dense orange clusters on logs; the orange color will stain your fingers when handled.

key_warnings: "Coral Spot". Tiny pinkish-red bumps on wood.
cap_description: None; forms tiny (1-2mm), pinhead-like fruiting bodies that are bright coral-pink to cinnabar red.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Absent; the tiny bumps are attached directly to the bark of dead twigs.
lookalikes: None; the tiny 'pink dots' on hardwood branches are very characteristic of this plant pathogen.
environment_tips: Extremely common on fallen branches of sycamore, beech, and horse chestnut.

habitat: Hardwood stumps and buried roots (especially oak)
key_warnings: "Jack-O'-Lantern". Causes severe, violent vomiting and cramps. Gills are bioluminescent. Often confused with Chanterelles.
cap_description: Large (5-20cm), convex then funnel-shaped; brilliant orange to pumpkin-orange; smooth.
gill_description: Decurrent, thin, and crowded; brilliant orange; glow faintly in total darkness.
stem_description: Tall, tapering toward the base; orange; grows in large, dense clusters from a central point.
smell: Unpleasant, often described as sweet but sickly or like overripe fruit.
lookalikes: Cantharellus cibarius (edible, false gills, white flesh, smells of apricots, grows singly on soil).
environment_tips: DANGER: Check the flesh; if it is orange throughout and growing in a cluster on wood, it is toxic.

key_warnings: "Western Jack-O'-Lantern". Highly toxic, causing severe gastrointestinal distress. Confused with Chanterelles.
cap_description: Large (5-18cm), funnel-shaped; olive-orange to dingy yellow-brown with olive tones.
gill_description: Decurrent, thin; orange with distinct olive-green tints; bioluminescent.
stem_description: Thick, tapering; olive-orange; grows in dense clusters at the base of trees.
lookalikes: Cantharellus californicus (Choice edible, much brighter yellow, false gills, white flesh).
environment_tips: Commonly found under Live Oak and Eucalyptus; the olive-green tint in the orange gills is diagnostic.

key_warnings: "Petticoat Mottlegill". Not actively sought; mild toxins.
cap_description: Small (1-4cm), bell-shaped; greyish-brown to tan; margin has distinct white, tooth-like veil fragments (the 'petticoat').
gill_description: Adnate, crowded; grey with black mottling from uneven spore maturation.
stem_description: Tall, slender, greyish-brown; brittle and straight.
lookalikes: Panaeolus cinctulus (hallucinogenic, has a darker band around the cap margin).
environment_tips: Found directly on old dung; the white veil fragments hanging from the cap edge are the best field mark.

key_warnings: "Bitter Oyster". Extremely astringent/bitter taste. The North American strain has bioluminescent gills.
cap_description: Small (1-3cm), fan-shaped; tan to cinnamon-brown; surface is scurfy or slightly hairy.
gill_description: Adnate to a lateral stem, crowded; light brown; the gills of North American specimens glow green in the dark.
stem_description: Very short, lateral, and tough; same color as the cap.
lookalikes: Pleurotus species (larger, white/lilac spores, not bitter).
environment_tips: Look for small tan 'ears' on logs; the taste is so bitter it will numb the tongue for minutes.

key_warnings: "Shield Lichen". No culinary value.
cap_description: Lichen thallus; forms grey-blue leafy rosettes; lobes have a distinct network of white lines (pseudocyphellae).
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Absent; underside is black with dark, root-like anchors (rhizines) that reach the edge.
lookalikes: Hypogymnia physodes (lobes are puffy and hollow).
environment_tips: One of the most common lichens on city trees; the white 'netted' lines on the blue-grey lobes are diagnostic.

habitat: Mixed woodlands, often near birch or pine
key_warnings: "Brown Roll-rim". Contains an antigen that builds up in the body over time, eventually causing fatal autoimmune hemolysis.
cap_description: Medium to large (5-15cm), convex then depressed; yellowish-brown to olive-brown; margin is deeply inrolled and fuzzy.
gill_description: Decurrent, crowded; yellowish, staining immediate dark brown when touched; easily rubbed off cap.
stem_description: Thick, brownish, often shorter than cap diameter; lacks a ring.
lookalikes: Lactarius species (exude milk, gills don't rub off cap easily).
environment_tips: DEADLY: The deeply inrolled, fuzzy cap margin and the dark brown staining of the yellow gills are critical warnings.

key_warnings: "Green Dog Lichen".
cap_description: Lichen thallus; large, leafy (foliose) and bright grass-green when wet, grey-green when dry; covered in small black bumps.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Absent; underside is white with a network of prominent veins and dark rhizines.
lookalikes: Peltigera britannica (similar, but black bumps are restricted to specific areas).
environment_tips: Common in mossy conifer forests; the bright green color when wet is very distinctive.

key_warnings: "Scaly Dog Lichen".
cap_description: Lichen thallus; greyish-brown to lead-grey; lobes have tiny, scale-like growths (isidia) along the margins and cracks.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Absent; underside has pale veins and long, slender rhizines.
lookalikes: Peltigera canina (lacks the scale-like isidia on the margins).
environment_tips: Often found growing over moss on damp logs or soil in shaded forests.

habitat: Roots and bases of living/dead conifers
key_warnings: "Dyer's Polypore". Parasitic; highly prized for dyeing wool brown/yellow/green, but not edible.
cap_description: Large (10-30cm), circular or bracket-like; velvety and yellowish-orange when young, becoming dark rusty-brown and corky.
gill_description: None; pores are large and yellowish, staining dark brown immediately where touched.
stem_description: Usually short, thick, and central or lateral; dark brown and velvety.
lookalikes: Inonotus species (grow on hardwood, not conifers).
environment_tips: Look for the velvety 'cow-pie' shaped mushroom at the base of old pines or Douglas-firs.

key_warnings: "Shadow Lichen". No culinary value.
cap_description: Lichen thallus; forms small (1-3cm), circular greyish-brown rosettes; center is often covered in blackish powder (soredia).
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Absent; underside is black with black rhizines.
lookalikes: Physcia species (usually have a white underside).
environment_tips: Very tolerant of air pollution; commonly found on tree trunks in urban centers.

key_warnings: "Common Stinkhorn". Edible when still inside its "egg" sac; smells like rotting meat when mature.
cap_description: Thimble-like head (3-5cm); covered in dark olive-green, foul-smelling slime; pitted underneath.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Tall (10-20cm), white, and very porous (like a sponge); emerges from a gelatinous white 'egg'.
smell: Incredibly foul, like rotting meat or sewage (can be smelled from yards away).
lookalikes: Morchella species (Morels; have a similar pitted head but never smell foul and lack the slime).
environment_tips: Follow your nose! If you smell rotting meat in the woods, look for the tall white stalk nearby.

key_warnings: "Willow Bracket". Extremely woody and hard.
cap_description: Large (10-30cm), hoof-shaped; greyish-black to black; surface is heavily cracked and deeply fissured.
gill_description: None; pore surface is cinnamon-brown; pores are tiny and multi-layered.
stem_description: Absent.
lookalikes: Fomes fomentarius (greyer, smoother surface, grows mostly on birch).
environment_tips: Almost exclusively found on willow; the black, 'burnt-looking' cracked surface is a key identifier.

key_warnings: "Aspen Bracket". Extremely woody; causes heart rot in aspen trees.
cap_description: Small to medium (5-15cm), triangular or hoof-shaped; dark greyish-brown to black; margin is often rounded and cinnamon-brown.
gill_description: None; underside is brownish with very tiny pores.
stem_description: Absent; grows out of the trunk of aspen trees.
lookalikes: Phellinus igniarius (larger, more cracked, associated with willow).
environment_tips: Exclusively found on Aspen (Populus tremuloides); look for brackets emerging from branch scars on the trunk.

key_warnings: "Wrinkled Crust". Flat, orange, wrinkled crust fungus.
cap_description: Crust-like (2-10cm); circular rosettes or irregular patches; brilliant orange to pinkish-orange; surface is deeply wrinkled and radiating from the center.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: Absent; attached flat to the wood surface.
lookalikes: Merulius tremellosus (paler, more gelatinous, white fuzzy margin).
environment_tips: Found on de-barked hardwood logs; the striking 'brain-like' wrinkles and bright orange color are unique.

habitat: Decaying hardwood and sometimes conifer wood
key_warnings: Too tough and gelatinous to be of interest for eating.
cap_description: Resupinate to reflexed; cap-like parts are hairy, white to orange-pink with a wavy margin.
gill_description: None; hymenium is wrinkled, folded, or pore-like, translucent orange-pink.
stem_description: None (attached directly to substrate).
lookalikes: Phlebia radiata (more orange, less hairy), Merulius tremellosus (synonym).
environment_tips: Often found on the underside of logs or on fallen branches.

habitat: Clustered on living or dead hardwoods
key_warnings: May cause gastrointestinal upset in some; slimy when wet.
cap_description: 4-15cm, convex to flat; slimy, golden-yellow to orange-brown with flattened brown scales.
gill_description: Attached, crowded; pale yellow, becoming rusty-brown with age.
stem_description: 5-10cm, yellow, often scaly below the ring zone; becomes rusty-brown at the base.
lookalikes: Pholiota squarrosa (drier, more scaly), Pholiota adiposa.
environment_tips: Commonly grows high up on tree trunks as well as at the base.

habitat: Clustered at the base of living or dead hardwoods and conifers
key_warnings: Causes gastrointestinal upset; often smells like garlic or onion.
cap_description: 3-12cm, convex to flat; dry, yellow to brownish-yellow, covered in prominent, recurved scales.
gill_description: Attached, crowded; greenish-yellow when young, becoming rusty-brown.
stem_description: 4-12cm, dry, scaly like the cap; pale yellow above the ring, brownish below.
smell: Strong, garlic-like, or sometimes like radish.
lookalikes: Pholiota aurivella (slimy), Pholiota squarrosoides (slimy cap).
environment_tips: Often found at the base of birches and aspens.

key_warnings: Unpleasant smell and tough texture; not poisonous but not edible.
cap_description: 2-8cm, fan-shaped; densely hairy, bright orange to pale yellow-orange.
gill_description: Radiating from the base; orange, crowded.
stem_description: None (attached laterally).
smell: Strong, unpleasant (like rotten cabbage or sulfur).
lookalikes: Pleurotus species (different colors, better smell), Tapinella atrotomentosa.
environment_tips: Can be found in large clusters on decaying logs.

habitat: Bark of deciduous trees, sometimes on rock or tombstones
key_warnings: Lichens are generally not edible and can accumulate toxins.
cap_description: Small (1-2cm), foliose; grey to white with inflated tips (hoods) and long cilia (hairs).
gill_description: None (Lichen).
stem_description: None (Lichen).
lookalikes: Physcia tenella (cilia but no hooded tips), Physcia stellaris.
environment_tips: Often found in sunny, nitrogen-enriched environments like bird perches.

habitat: Bark and branches of conifers and hardwoods
key_warnings: Lichens are generally not edible.
cap_description: Large, foliose; pale grey-green to blue-grey, underside black or brown, margins frilly/crisped.
gill_description: None (Lichen).
stem_description: None (Lichen).
lookalikes: Cetrelia species, Parmotrema species.
environment_tips: Very common in moist, cool forests.

key_warnings: Ensure they are fresh; check for oyster mushroom flies.
cap_description: 5-20cm, oyster-shaped; smooth, white to grey to brown, margin often wavy.
gill_description: Decurrent, crowded; white to cream, often running down the stem.
stem_description: Short or absent, lateral and thick.
smell: Mild, oyster-like or slightly of anise.
lookalikes: Pleurotus pulmonarius (summer/warmer weather), Omphalotus illudens (toxic, orange).
environment_tips: Found on logs and stumps after rain in cooler months.

key_warnings: Very similar to P. ostreatus but prefers warmer temperatures.
cap_description: 3-10cm, oyster-shaped; pale white to cream or tan, thinner than P. ostreatus.
gill_description: Decurrent, crowded; white to yellowish with age.
stem_description: Short, lateral, often hairy at the base.
lookalikes: Pleurotus ostreatus (thicker, cooler weather), Pleurocybella porrigens (toxic, on conifer).
environment_tips: Look for these on sunny days after rain in early summer.

habitat: Lawns, woodchips, and near buried wood
key_warnings: Very fragile; difficult to identify with certainty due to variability.
cap_description: 3-8cm, convex to flat; honey-yellow when wet, fading to white/cream when dry, often with veil remnants at margin.
gill_description: Attached, crowded; white, then pinkish-grey, finally dark brown.
stem_description: 4-10cm, thin, white, hollow, and very fragile.
lookalikes: Other Psathyrella species, Agrocybe praecox.
environment_tips: Very common in urban areas and gardens.

habitat: Bark of conifers and hardwoods in clean air areas
key_warnings: Lichens are generally not edible.
cap_description: Foliose/Fruticose; grey-white to blue-grey, strap-shaped lobes with isidia (tiny outgrowths), underside black/dark.
gill_description: None (Lichen).
stem_description: None (Lichen).
lookalikes: Evernia prunastri (greenish underside, softer), Physcia species.
environment_tips: Sensitive to air pollution; used in the perfume industry.

key_warnings: Gelatinous texture is off-putting to some; bland flavor.
cap_description: 2-6cm, tongue or spoon-shaped; translucent white to grey-brown, jelly-like.
gill_description: None; underside is covered in tiny white, gelatinous teeth/spines.
stem_description: Short or lateral, often absent, gelatinous.
lookalikes: Various jelly fungi (but the teeth/spines are unique).
environment_tips: Often found on very rotten conifer logs.

habitat: Coastal dunes on wood debris and grasses
key_warnings: Extremely high psilocybin content; illegal in many regions; may cause Wood Lover's Paralysis.
cap_description: 3-10cm, conical to convex with a prominent umbo; chestnut brown, hygrophanous (fades to straw-yellow), bruises blue.
gill_description: Attached; brown to dark purple-brown.
stem_description: 9-15cm, white, silky, bruises blue intensely when touched.
lookalikes: Galerina marginata (Deadly), other Psilocybe species.
environment_tips: Restricted to coastal regions; prefers cold temperatures.

habitat: Disturbed soils, landslides, and areas with high humidity
key_warnings: Contains psilocybin; illegal in many regions; careful of lookalikes.
cap_description: 2-7cm, convex; brownish-yellow to brown, hygrophanous, bruises blue-green on the margin.
gill_description: Attached; whitish, becoming dark purple-brown.
stem_description: 5-9cm, white to brownish, bruises blue when damaged.
lookalikes: Psilocybe cubensis, various Inocybe species (Toxic).
environment_tips: Often found in landslide areas in Mexico where soil is disturbed.

key_warnings: Contains psilocybin; illegal in many regions; avoid confusing with toxic dung-loving species.
cap_description: 2-8cm, conic to convex; golden-yellow to brownish, smooth, bruises blue when touched.
gill_description: Attached; greyish, becoming dark purple-grey to black.
stem_description: 4-15cm, white to yellowish, bruises blue; persistent ring (annulus) present.
lookalikes: Protostropharia semiglobata, various toxic Chlorophyllum species.
environment_tips: Most commonly found in cow pastures after warm rains.

habitat: Woodchips, mulch, and landscaped garden beds
key_warnings: Highly psychoactive; illegal in many regions; can be confused with deadly Galerina.
cap_description: 2-5cm, convex with a wavy margin; chestnut brown fading to buff, bruises blue prominently.
gill_description: Attached; brown, becoming dark purple-brown.
stem_description: 3-6cm, white, silky, bruises blue.
lookalikes: Galerina marginata (Deadly, no blue bruising, rusty spores), Psilocybe allenii.
environment_tips: Often found in urban parks where woodchips have been applied.

habitat: Floodplains, wood debris near riverbanks and streams
key_warnings: Contains psilocybin; illegal in many regions; distinct for its spring fruiting.
cap_description: 1-4.5cm, convex to subumbonate; orangish-brown to brownish-grey, bruises blue.
gill_description: Attached; whitish to lavender-grey, then dark purple-brown.
stem_description: 3-9cm, white to brownish, bruises blue; often has a faint ring zone.
lookalikes: Psilocybe caerulipes, Galerina marginata (Deadly).
environment_tips: Often found among box elder and sycamore trees in flood zones.

habitat: Disturbed forest soils, mossy areas, and logging roads
key_warnings: Contains psilocybin; lower potency than P. cyanescens; illegal in many regions.
cap_description: 0.5-2cm, conical to bell-shaped; dull brown, hygrophanous, bruises slightly blue on the margin.
gill_description: Attached; cinnamon brown to dark brown.
stem_description: 4-8cm, thin, brownish, slightly scaly at the base, bruises blue-green.
lookalikes: Mycena species, Galerina marginata (Deadly).
environment_tips: Prefers mossy ground in coniferous forests.

key_warnings: Sometimes bitter, though not toxic; distinct yellow flesh.
cap_description: 4-15cm, convex; grey-brown to olive-yellow, dry, smooth.
gill_description: Pores (not gills); bright yellow, becoming olive-gold, not bruising blue.
stem_description: 5-15cm, bright yellow, covered in a prominent, raised net-like pattern (reticulation).
lookalikes: Retiboletus griseus (greyer stem), various bitter Tylopilus species.
environment_tips: Commonly found in mixed deciduous forests.

habitat: Living leaves of maple trees (Acer species)
key_warnings: A fungal pathogen (Tar Spot); not a mushroom in the culinary sense.
cap_description: Black, raised, crust-like spots (1-2cm) on maple leaves.
gill_description: None (ascomycete).
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Other tar spot fungi like Rhytisma punctatum.
environment_tips: Indicates good air quality as it is sensitive to sulfur dioxide.

key_warnings: Some reports suggest it may contain toxins if not cooked thoroughly; bitter skin.
cap_description: 3-10cm, fan-shaped; olive-green to yellow-brown, slimy when wet, velvety when dry.
