gill_description: Attached/Decurrent; yellowish to orange, crowded, meeting the stem abruptly.
stem_description: Very short, lateral, yellowish and scaly.
lookalikes: Pleurotus ostreatus (different colors, no olive tint), Panellus stipticus (small, toxic).
environment_tips: One of the few edible mushrooms found during freezes in late autumn.

habitat: Dead hardwood twigs and branches buried in leaf litter
key_warnings: Tough texture; mostly used for decoration in salads.
cap_description: 2-5cm, cup-shaped; inner surface brilliant scarlet red, outer surface pale pink/white and fuzzy.
gill_description: None (cup fungus).
stem_description: Short or absent, white.
lookalikes: Sarcoscypha coccinea (requires microscopy to distinguish).
environment_tips: One of the first fungi to appear in spring, often while snow is still on the ground.

habitat: Conifer forests, among moss and needles
key_warnings: Listed as threatened in many regions; do not pick.
cap_description: 3-10cm, round to cup-shaped; dark brown, velvety, filled with a clear gelatinous fluid.
gill_description: None (cup fungus).
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Bulgaria inquinans (smaller, on wood).
environment_tips: Often buried in moss, making it hard to spot.

habitat: Dead hardwoods, sometimes on living trees or stored wood
key_warnings: Extremely tough; known to cause rare respiratory infections in immunocompromised people.
cap_description: 1-4cm, fan-shaped; hairy, white to greyish, margin split and rolled inwards.
gill_description: Radiating; white to pinkish, distinctively 'split' longitudinally.
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: None, the split gills are unique.
environment_tips: One of the most widely distributed fungi in the world.

key_warnings: Tough and woody; not toxic but inedible.
cap_description: 1-4cm, shelf-like; hairy (hirsute), zoned with orange, yellow, and grey colors.
gill_description: None; underside is smooth and bright orange/yellow.
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Stereum ostrea (larger, less hairy), Trametes versicolor (has pores).
environment_tips: Does not turn red when bruised, unlike Stereum sanguinolentum.

key_warnings: Tough and leathery.
cap_description: 2-7cm, fan-shaped; zoned with brown, orange, and red-brown, resembles a turkey tail but smooth underneath.
gill_description: None; underside is smooth, greyish-buff to yellowish.
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Trametes versicolor (has pores), Stereum hirsutum (smaller, more hairy).
environment_tips: Often grows in overlapping clusters on logs.

habitat: Woodchips, leaf litter, and grassy areas near wood
key_warnings: The slimy blue coating is often considered unappetizing; easy to confuse with others.
cap_description: 3-8cm, convex; strikingly blue-green, slimy, fading to yellow-green, often with white veil scales.
gill_description: Attached; pale grey, then dark purple-brown with white edges.
stem_description: 4-10cm, blue-green, scaly below the ring.
lookalikes: Stropharia caerulea (fewer scales, different gill edge).
environment_tips: Loses its blue color quickly in dry weather.

habitat: Forest litter and woodchips in coniferous forests
key_warnings: Not known to be toxic, but generally considered poor quality.
cap_description: 5-15cm, convex to flat; pale yellow, slimy when wet, with white cottony veil fragments hanging from the margin.
gill_description: Attached; greyish, becoming dark purple-brown.
stem_description: 8-18cm, white, shaggy/scaly below the ring zone.
lookalikes: Leratiomyces percevalii, Stropharia coronilla.
environment_tips: Common in the coastal forests of the Pacific Northwest.

key_warnings: Can cause contact dermatitis in sensitive individuals; slimy cap skin should be removed.
cap_description: 3-10cm, yellow with reddish-brown spots/scales, very slimy when wet.
gill_description: Pores; large and angular, yellow, not bruising blue.
stem_description: 3-9cm, thin, yellow with reddish dots, no ring.
lookalikes: Suillus sibiricus, Suillus granulatus.
environment_tips: Almost always found under five-needle pines.

key_warnings: Remove the slimy cap skin to avoid gastrointestinal upset.
cap_description: 4-12cm, convex; reddish-brown to yellow-brown, very slimy, smooth.
gill_description: Pores; small, yellow, exuding milky droplets when young.
stem_description: 4-8cm, pale yellow with small pinkish or brownish granules near the top; no ring.
lookalikes: Suillus luteus (has a ring), Suillus americanus (dots are different).
environment_tips: One of the most common Suillus species.

key_warnings: Slimy cap skin should be removed; flavor is mild.
cap_description: 5-10cm, convex; bright yellow, orange, or reddish-brown, very slimy.
gill_description: Pores; yellow, bruising reddish-brown, often covered by a yellow veil when young.
stem_description: 5-10cm, yellow to reddish-brown, with a distinct whitish or yellowish ring.
lookalikes: Suillus clintonianus, Suillus luteus.
environment_tips: If there are no larch trees nearby, it is not this species.

key_warnings: Peel the slimy skin; the ring is large and purplish underneath.
cap_description: 5-12cm, convex; dark brown to chocolate brown, extremely slimy.
gill_description: Pores; small, yellow, becoming olive-yellow.
stem_description: 4-10cm, white to yellowish with a large, membrane-like ring that is often dark purple.
lookalikes: Suillus granulatus (no ring), Suillus grevillei.
environment_tips: Often found in large numbers in pine plantations.

key_warnings: Also known as Suillus pictus; less slimy than other Suillus.
cap_description: 3-12cm, convex; covered in reddish-pink fibrillose scales on a yellow background.
gill_description: Pores; yellow, angular, bruising brownish, covered by a cottony veil when young.
stem_description: 4-10cm, scaly like the cap, with a fuzzy ring.
lookalikes: Suillus cavipes (hollow stem base).
environment_tips: Very easy to identify due to its bright red-scaly cap and association with white pine.

key_warnings: Contains toxins that can cause gastrointestinal distress; distinct velvet stem.
cap_description: 5-20cm, fan to kidney shaped; brown, dry, velvety when young, margin rolled in.
gill_description: Decurrent, crowded; yellowish, often wavy or branched.
stem_description: Short, thick, lateral, and covered in dense, dark brown velvet.
lookalikes: Paxillus involutus (Toxic, no velvet stem).
environment_tips: Almost always found growing on well-decayed conifer wood.

key_warnings: Tough and woody; also known as Lenzites betulina.
cap_description: 2-10cm, shelf-like; zoned with grey, white, and brown, velvety/hairy.
gill_description: Gills (distinctive for a polypore); white to cream, thick and leathery.
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Trametes versicolor (has pores), Daedaleopsis confragosa.
environment_tips: The only Trametes-like fungus with true gills.

key_warnings: Tough and woody; often green due to algae.
cap_description: 5-20cm, shelf-like; white to grey, velvety, with a distinct 'hump' (gibbous) at the attachment point.
gill_description: Pores; elongated, slot-like (daedaleoid), white.
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Trametes elegans, Daedaleopsis confragosa.
environment_tips: The elongated pores are a key identifying feature.

key_warnings: Tough and woody.
cap_description: 2-10cm, shelf-like; zoned with white, grey, and tan, very hairy (hirsute).
gill_description: Pores; round, white to greyish, 3-4 per mm.
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Trametes versicolor (less hairy, more colorful), Trametes pubescens (less hairy).
environment_tips: Often has a thicker, more rigid margin than T. versicolor.

key_warnings: Tough and woody.
cap_description: 2-5cm, shelf-like; zoned with ochre, grey, and brown, velvety, thicker at the base than T. versicolor.
gill_description: Pores; round, white to cream.
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Trametes versicolor (thinner, more colorful), Trametes hirsuta.
environment_tips: Lack of blue or black zones helps distinguish it from T. versicolor.

key_warnings: Too tough to eat; used in teas for medicinal purposes (Turkey Tail).
cap_description: 2-8cm, shelf-like; multicolored zones (brown, blue, orange, white), velvety.
gill_description: Pores; very small (3-5 per mm), white to cream, bruising slightly.
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Stereum ostrea (no pores), Trametes hirsuta (hairy, less colorful).
environment_tips: True Turkey Tail has visible pores on the underside, unlike the 'False' Turkey Tail.

key_warnings: Gelatinous and bland; also known as Witches' Butter.
cap_description: 2-10cm, lobed and brain-like; bright yellow to orange, jelly-like, dries to a thin crust.
gill_description: None (jelly fungus).
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Dacrymyces chrysospermus (grows on conifer), Tremella aurantia.
environment_tips: Commonly found on fallen oak branches.

key_warnings: Tough and leathery.
cap_description: 1-5cm, shelf-like, often in large overlapping clusters; grey-white, zoned, margin often lilac/purple when fresh.
gill_description: Pores (becoming tooth-like with age); strikingly purple when young, fading to brown.
stem_description: None.
lookalikes: Trichaptum abietinum (on conifers), Trametes versicolor.
environment_tips: The purple pore surface is the best field mark.

key_warnings: The American Matsutake; high culinary value; careful of toxic white Tricholomas.
cap_description: 5-20cm, convex; white with brownish scales, firm, margin rolled in when young.
gill_description: Attached; white, bruising slightly brown.
stem_description: 5-15cm, thick, white, with a cottony ring that separates the smooth top from the scaly base.
smell: Strong, distinctive (like spicy cinnamon and old socks).
lookalikes: Tricholoma magnivelare, Amanita smithiana (Toxic).
environment_tips: Highly sought after; often buried deep in the duff.

key_warnings: Distinctive 'Plums and Custard' colors; generally considered poor tasting.
cap_description: 5-12cm, convex; covered in dense, plum-red to purplish scales over a yellow background.
gill_description: Attached; bright yellow, crowded.
stem_description: 5-10cm, yellow, covered in purplish scales like the cap.
lookalikes: Tricholomopsis decora (no purple).
environment_tips: One of the most colorful mushrooms found on conifer wood.

key_warnings: Bitter Bolete; even one can ruin a whole dish; not toxic but inedible.
cap_description: 5-15cm, convex; brown to tan, smooth.
gill_description: Pores; white, becoming pinkish with age, bruising brownish.
stem_description: 5-15cm, thick, with a prominent, dark brown raised net-like pattern (reticulation).
lookalikes: Boletus edulis (white reticulation, tastes mild/nutty).
environment_tips: If in doubt, a tiny taste of the flesh will confirm the bitterness.

key_warnings: Bitter flavor; not toxic.
cap_description: 6-20cm, convex; dark reddish-brown to purple-brown, smooth.
gill_description: Pores; white, becoming pinkish/flesh-colored.
stem_description: 8-20cm, thick, brownish, smooth or slightly reticulated at the very top.
lookalikes: Tylopilus felleus, Tylopilus badiceps (Edible).
environment_tips: The reddish-brown cap is darker than T. felleus.

key_warnings: Tough and leathery; also known as Devil's Urn.
cap_description: 3-10cm, deep cup-shaped; black to dark brown, velvety, margin often tattered.
gill_description: None (cup fungus).
stem_description: Short, black, attached to wood.
lookalikes: None, very distinctive early spring fungus.
environment_tips: Often appears at the same time and place as morels.

habitat: Damp areas under cottonwood, aspen, and willow
key_warnings: Early Morel; can cause gastrointestinal upset or loss of coordination in some people; must be cooked well.
cap_description: 2-5cm, thimble-like; wrinkled/pitted, brown, attached only at the very top of the stem.
gill_description: None.
stem_description: 5-15cm, white to yellowish, brittle, hollow or filled with cottony fibers.
lookalikes: Morchella species (Morels - cap is attached to stem), Verpa conica.
environment_tips: Often found just before true morels appear.

habitat: Disturbed soil, gardens, compost, and fields
key_warnings: Be careful not to confuse with toxic Amanita species; check for lack of a ring and pink spores.
cap_description: 5-15cm, convex to flat; grey to white, very slimy when wet.
gill_description: Free, crowded; white, becoming pink as spores mature.
stem_description: 8-20cm, white, smooth, with a sack-like volva at the base; no ring.
lookalikes: Amanita phalloides (Toxic, has a ring, white spores), Pluteus cervinus.
environment_tips: Commonly fruits in enriched garden soil.

habitat: Bark of conifers and birch trees
key_warnings: Contains vulpinic acid, which is toxic; used historically to poison wolves.
cap_description: Foliose; bright yellow to greenish-yellow, margins with yellow soredia (powdery dots).
gill_description: None (Lichen).
stem_description: None (Lichen).
lookalikes: Vulpicida canadensis, Xanthoria parietina.
environment_tips: Very bright yellow color is a warning of its toxicity.

habitat: Bark, rocks, and walls, especially near the sea or bird colonies
key_warnings: Common Orange Lichen.
cap_description: Foliose; bright orange to yellow-orange, lobes wide and flat, often with cup-shaped fruiting bodies (apothecia).
gill_description: None (Lichen).
stem_description: None (Lichen).
lookalikes: Caloplaca species, Vulpicida pinastri.
environment_tips: Highly tolerant of nitrogen pollution.
